question.question:
Revenue is 4140000 USD per year and cost of sales is 56 percent of revenue; both stay unchanged. Use a 365-day year for every days ratio. Receivable days are measured on revenue, inventory days on cost of sales, and payable days on purchases. In the base year inventory was flat, so base-year purchases equal cost of sales. A working-capital program cuts receivable days by 14 days (a negative cut means receivable days rise), moves inventory days from 39 to 74, and moves payable days from 40 to 30. Purchases in the program year equal cost of sales plus the change in the inventory balance from base to target. Cash released equals the fall in receivables plus the fall in inventory plus the rise in payables, each measured as base balance versus target balance. Compute the net cash released by the program, in USD.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd` with no unit label or additional text.

Cash released by the change in the inventory balance.
Purchases in the program year after the inventory change.
Rise in the payables balance from base to target.
